gaps.sentence: Be careful not to ___ the medicine — read the label twice (USE).
gaps.explanation: The prefix mis- means wrongly: misuse means to use something incorrectly. A base verb follows 'not to'.

gaps.sentence: He had a happy ___ in the countryside (CHILD).
gaps.hint: noun needed: the period of being a child (-hood)
gaps.explanation: The suffix -hood forms period-of-life nouns: childhood.

gaps.sentence: The team played ___ and deserved to win (EXCELLENT).
gaps.explanation: An adverb modifies the verb 'played': excellently (-ly).

gaps.sentence: The campaign aims to raise ___ of road safety (AWARE).
gaps.explanation: The suffix -ness forms the noun: raise awareness is the fixed phrase; 'aware' is an adjective.

gaps.sentence: The soup tastes a bit ___ ; add some salt (TASTE).
gaps.explanation: The suffix -less means without: tasteless explains why salt is needed. An adjective follows 'tastes'.

gaps.sentence: The ___ (INVENT) of the new engine worked day and night.
gaps.explanation: The person who worked day and night is the inventor; 'invention' is the thing created.

gaps.sentence: He denied all knowledge of the ___ (APPEAR) of the documents.
gaps.explanation: The documents vanished, so the negative noun 'disappearance' is needed; 'appearance' means coming into view.

gaps.hint: person needed (-ist for fields of study)
gaps.explanation: The suffix -ist forms the person who studies a subject: biology becomes biologist.
